title: A comparison of methods for estimating the lactate threshold
publisher: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
claims: The study compared four field methods with a laboratory 4.0 mmol/L blood lactate criterion in 27 competitive distance runners and triathletes.
Mean estimated running speeds from the 30-minute time trial (SEE 0.21 m/s) and the VDOT method (SEE 0.41 m/s) did not differ significantly from the laboratory criterion (P>0.05).
The 30-minute time trial estimate of heart rate at lactate threshold did not differ significantly from the criterion (SEE 8.0 b/min), and the authors suggest coaches should consider it.
